title: Orchestrated Subnet Topology Terraform Reconciler with Endpoint-aware Routing & Health Probes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module and reconciliation pattern to manage subnet topologies, AZ-aware NAT/IGW placement, VPC endpoints (interface + gateway), and route table orchestration for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support non-disruptive upgrades, automatic synthetic health probes for egress routes, and a safe rollout strategy for changes that affect route tables or NAT/IGW attachments. Goals: reduce manual drift, enable canary applies for topology changes, provide actionable metrics (route health, endpoint reachability), and expose clear inputs for customers to pin subnets and control egress patterns. This ticket covers: module design, core terraform code, CI/CD validation (plan/apply gating), a lightweight lambda probe for route validation, and documentation + examples for private customers.
tasks: Design module API: inputs for subnet roles, AZ preferences, NAT mode (single-igw | per-az-nat-gateway | nat-gateway-pool), endpoint templates and route table assignments
Implement Terraform module: subnets, route tables, nat_gateways/igw resources, interface_gateway endpoints, s3/gateway endpoints, and tags for ownership
Add reconciliation patterns: terraform-import-friendly naming, preserves route table IDs to avoid destructive replaces, and plan-time validation checks
Build health check Lambda + CloudWatch synthetic probe for each egress path (ICMP/tcp handshake to a stable external IP and attempt endpoint DNS resolution)
Create CI pipeline changes: plan validation, run-time drift detection job, and gated apply that supports "canary_az" variable to limit first rollout
Add automated rollback guides and destroy-safe strategies in README
Author unit and integration tests: terratest for module with mocked AWS account, and small-scale smoke test in staging
Publish example usage for Private deployment templates and Console integration (route-level tags for Console dashboards)
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs for subnet roles (control-plane, nodes/compute, ingress, egress) and creates matching route tables
Supports both gateway endpoints (S3/Dynamo) and interface endpoints with stable security group patterns
Non-disruptive update path verified: changing a route target uses replace-with-minimal-downtime plan (canary_az applied)
Health probe Lambda reports per-route status to CloudWatch metrics and alerts when > 2 AZs show failure for 5m
Terraform plan/apply guardrails in CI prevent accidental mass-replacement of NAT/IGW unless 'force_replace' is explicitly set and reviewed
Module documented with example Private deployment template and a migration guide for existing customers using older vpc modules
notes: Decision: prefer NAT gateway per AZ for high-throughput Private deployments by default, with an opt-in single-IGW+NAT combination for cost-sensitive tenants
Trade-off: per-AZ NAT reduces cross-AZ data transfer but increases resource count; will provide an opt-in pooling mode
Compatibility: module must be compatible with existing customer VPCs by supporting passing existing subnet IDs and route table IDs
Upgrade strategy: detect when route table associations would change; perform canary apply in one AZ and monitor health metrics before full rollout
Risk: interface endpoints require customer-managed security group rules; include a helper template that creates minimal SGs and documents required egress IP ranges for probe targets
